title: Install and use the sql plugin (SQLite)

steps.task: Add the tauri-plugin-sql crate to the Rust backend's dependencies in `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`.
Register the sql plugin with the app builder in `lib.rs`.

mutations.diff:
--- a/src-tauri/src/lib.rs
+++ b/src-tauri/src/lib.rs
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@
 pub fn run() {
     tauri::Builder::default()
         .plugin(tauri_plugin_opener::init())
+        .plugin(tauri_plugin_sql::Builder::default().build())
         .invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![greet])
         .run(tauri::generate_context!())
         .expect("error while running tauri application");

steps.task: Install the JavaScript guest bindings package with the project's package manager, then make sure the frontend still builds.
Enable the SQLite driver: the plugin compiles a database engine only when its Cargo feature is enabled. The backend must build with the plugin registered.
From the frontend, load `sqlite:test.db` and run an INSERT with the "$#" substitution syntax. The TypeScript build must stay green.
Define an initial migration creating a `todos` table and register it on the plugin builder for the `sqlite:test.db` connection. The backend must keep compiling.

mutations.diff:
--- a/src-tauri/src/lib.rs
+++ b/src-tauri/src/lib.rs
@@ -1,3 +1,5 @@
+use tauri_plugin_sql::{Migration, MigrationKind};
+
 // Learn more about Tauri commands at https://tauri.app/develop/calling-rust/
 #[tauri::command]
 fn greet(name: &str) -> String {
@@ -6,9 +8,23 @@
 
 #[cfg_attr(mobile, tauri::mobile_entry_point)]
 pub fn run() {
+    let migrations = vec![
+        // Define your migrations here
+        Migration {
+            version: 1,
+            description: "create_initial_tables",
+            sql: "CREATE TABLE todos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, status TEXT);",
+            kind: MigrationKind::Up,
+        },
+    ];
+
     tauri::Builder::default()
         .plugin(tauri_plugin_opener::init())
-        .plugin(tauri_plugin_sql::Builder::default().build())
+        .plugin(
+            tauri_plugin_sql::Builder::default()
+                .add_migrations("sqlite:test.db", migrations)
+                .build(),
+        )
         .invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![greet])
         .run(tauri::generate_context!())
         .expect("error while running tauri application");

steps.task: Apply the migrations when the app starts by preloading the database connection in `tauri.conf.json`.
Let the frontend use the database: loading it from the webview must be denied before the capability grants the sql permissions and succeed after — and loading applies the migrations.
